newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus studying implications of Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger.
newsitem.headline: Airbus studying implications of Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger.

text.p: European plane-making consortium Airbus Industrie confirmed Wednesday that it was reviewing the antitrust implications of a planned merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp.
"We are looking at the long-term implications. For the time being, I can't comment further," a spokeswoman said.

Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Airbus's A3XX super-jumbo project director, Juergen Thomas, said he believed Boeing's recent scepticism about such a project reflected dissatisfaction with its own 747-stretch design rather than insufficient market demand.
He said he expected Seattle-based Boeing, the world's largest commercial aircraft maker, to return to that segment of the market.
The Airbus spokeswoman also confirmed that Italian manufacturer Alenia and Saab of Sweden were interested in investing in its project to build a 555-seat jet, which Airbus expects to cost $8 billion.
Airbus aims to formally launch the super-jumbo plane in December 1998 for delivery in 2003.
The spokeswoman said that Alenia had not signed an agreement but that "they have expressed interest.
Saab has also expressed its interest very strongly recently," she said.
The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Alenia planned to take a 10 percent stake in the project and Saab was close to signing an agreement to take up to 5 percent.
Thomas told the Journal that a Korean consortium also had expressed interest and his "personal guess" was that they would take between 5 percent and 10 percent.
Korean officials from Samsung, Daewoo, Korean Air and Hyundai visited Airbus's Toulouse headquarters last month to discuss the project.

About 33 percent of the project's financing is expected to come from aid from European governments, 40 percent from risk-sharing partners in Europe and Asia, and the rest from the Airbus consortium partners -- Aerospatiale of France, Daimler-Benz of Germany, British Aerospace Plc and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
